rounds.text: Rakan Steels Ltd is currently demonstrating an extraordinary inflection in operational efficiency, evidenced by a 10-year compounded profit growth of 65% [E5] that has accelerated to a staggering 2564% over the trailing twelve months [E6]. This explosive profitability is underpinned by a massive expansion in operating margins, which climbed from 3% to 18% over the last three years [E8]. The company’s ability to generate wealth is further confirmed by a robust ROE of 45.3% [E2] and a ROCE of 40.7% [E1], both of which indicate highly efficient capital allocation. While long-term sales growth has been a steady 12% [E3], the recent 91% surge in trailing twelve-month sales [E4] suggests the business has reached a significant new scale. Conceded: [E9]. Despite the volatility shown in the most recent quarterly margin [E9], the broader multi-year trend of margin expansion and profit growth highlights a business that is fundamentally outperforming its historical baseline [E5, E8].

The recent financial performance of Rakan Steels Ltd exhibits extreme volatility that undermines the sustainability of its historical growth metrics. While the company reports impressive long-term compounded profit growth of 65% [E5], the most recent quarterly data reveals a catastrophic collapse in profitability, with operating margins plummeting to -427% in March 2026 from 10% in the year-ago quarter [E9]. This massive 437 percentage point swing suggests that the recent trailing twelve-month profit growth of 2564% [E6] is likely an anomaly rather than a reliable indicator of future earnings power. Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E4], [E7], and [E8]. Relying on long-term averages or trailing twelve-month figures ignores the severe and immediate deterioration in operational efficiency evidenced by the latest quarterly results [E9]. Consequently, the current valuation, if predicated on recent explosive growth, fails to account for the sudden and profound instability in the company's core business model [E9].

The bear’s characterization of the company as fundamentally unstable ignores the massive structural improvement in profitability evidenced by the expansion of operating margins from 3% to 18% over the last three years [E8]. While the bear highlights a single quarterly margin contraction [E9], this isolated data point is mathematically inconsistent with the company’s demonstrated ability to generate a 40.7% ROCE and a 45.3% ROE [E1, E2]. Conceded: [E9]. The bear’s focus on one quarter fails to reconcile with the 2564% profit growth achieved over the trailing twelve months, which confirms that the business is currently operating at a scale and efficiency level far superior to its historical baseline [E6]. By dismissing the 91% sales growth [E4] and the 65% long-term profit growth [E5] as anomalies, the bear overlooks the clear trend of compounding value that has defined the company’s trajectory. The recent quarterly volatility [E9] does not negate the fact that the company maintains a median return on equity of 45% [E7], proving that the business model remains highly productive over the relevant time horizons.

The bull’s reliance on trailing twelve-month profit growth [E6] and annual margin expansion [E8] ignores the catastrophic reality of the most recent data, which reveals a quarterly operating margin of -427% [E9]. Conceded: [E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8]. While the bull dismisses this quarterly collapse as an isolated anomaly, a swing of -437 percentage points in a single year [E9] indicates a business model that is currently hemorrhaging value rather than compounding it. The historical averages of 40.7% ROCE and 45.3% ROE [E1, E2] are rendered backward-looking and potentially irrelevant when contrasted with the extreme volatility and negative margins reported in the most recent quarter [E9]. By prioritizing long-term growth figures [E5] over the immediate, severe deterioration in operating efficiency [E9], the bull fails to address the risk that the company’s recent performance is not a trend of value creation, but a precursor to structural instability. The massive discrepancy between annual profitability and the latest quarterly loss [E8, E9] suggests that the company’s current trajectory is unsustainable and fundamentally broken.
